body: This somehow bisects to #106661. I've checked a couple times because a cursory glance at the PR makes it seem basically equivalent, but perhaps there's an extra copy happening somewhere now or something? CC @KirbyRider1337

Hi, I am posting this in both this issue and also #105248 since both affected the same MRP and since both issues have been merged into the same new Godot version (beta 4) it is not straight forward to know exactly how much each of them contributed to the fix. First of all thank you for solving this issue!! I don't want to be picky but since I have been following this sort of performance regression since Godot 4.3 I thought I would leave here my tests now after the fix. Maybe some performance lost since 4.3 is acceptable for this specific scenarios since many things were added to the engine since then and this trade off is acceptable, but I just wanted to let you know that there seems to still be a significant difference from what 4.3 was able to do and keep in mind that the more collisions are visible the more the performance difference would probably since it seems to be more about how Godot handles very large number of visible collisions and the performance quickly degrades after reaching a high number. This is the MRP I used for my tests. You just need to download them (one is for Godot 4.3 and the other for any version of Godot 4.5 but it is just the same scene), enable the Visible Collision Shapes toggle and hit the Run Project button. To make things equal in Godot 4.5 I disabled the "Embed Game" option for running the project. [collisions-MRP-1-Godot4.3.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21526975/collisions-MRP-1-Godot4.3.zip) [collisions-MRP-1-Godot4.5.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21526976/collisions-MRP-1-Godot4.5.zip) Results: This shows the improvement since I reported #108435 which was a big regression. This shows the improvement between 4.5.dev4 (before regression #108435) and the latest beta: Finally here I compare 4.3 with the latest beta, 4.3 still runs faster, around a 20% faster: This is a small difference now, but still significant, so I hope my report is useful. Thanks again.
I've reopened #105248 to track the rest of the performance regression from 4.3 mentioned in @diegopau's latest comment.
